Hyperbolic invariant set

Words: 75
Dynamical systems OurBigBook.com
A compact invariant set K of a smooth invertible map f is uniformly hyperbolic when its tangent spaces split continuously as Es⊕Eu, the derivative preserves this splitting, and constants C>0, 0<ρ<1 satisfy ∥Dfnvs​∥≤Cρn∥vs​∥ and ∥Df−nvu​∥≤Cρn∥vu​∥ for every n≥0. Thus the stable direction contracts forward and the unstable direction contracts backward. A Smale horseshoe is an example with nontrivial symbolic dynamics; such a set can contain infinitely many saddle periodic orbits without attracting an open neighborhood.

Smale horseshoe

Words: 87
Dynamical systems OurBigBook.com
A Smale horseshoe is a compact hyperbolic invariant set of a smooth map with expanding and contracting directions and at least two strips that stretch across a common rectangle. Iterating the strips and their inverse images produces a Cantor-set product on which the dynamics are conjugate to a full shift. It supplies infinitely many saddle periodic orbits and chaotic itineraries; hyperbolicity alone does not make it an attracting invariant set. The geometric construction explains why phase-dependent reinjection near a Shilnikov bifurcation can create chaos even when the associated symmetric amplitude equations have no such mechanism.

Equivariant dynamical system (F(gx,μ)=gF(x,μ))

Words: 1k Articles: 17
Dynamical systems OurBigBook.com
An equivariant dynamical system has a vector field commuting with the action of a symmetry group. Its flow map preserves every subgroup's fixed-point subspace, because equivariance and uniqueness keep initial states fixed by that subgroup. Polynomial normal forms are constrained by the weights and parity of the group representation.

Translation invariants of Fourier-mode phases (n⋅θ,∑j​nj​qj​=0)

Words: 125 Articles: 1
Equivariant dynamical system OurBigBook.com
If a translation symmetry acts on complex Fourier modes by Aj​↦eiqj​⋅sAj​, a linear combination of their phases is invariant precisely when its coefficient vector lies in the kernel of the matrix of wavevectors. For four amplitudes whose wavevectors span a plane, this leaves two independent phase variables after quotienting translations. At zero amplitude, polar phases are undefined, so smooth centre manifold equations should first be written in Cartesian amplitudes.

Wavevector selection rule for equivariant monomials (∑j​(pj​−qj​)kj​=kℓ​)

Words: 66
Translation invariants of Fourier-mode phases OurBigBook.com
An equivariant dynamical system can contain the monomial ∏j​Ajpj​​Ajqj​​ in its ℓth amplitude equation only if its total wavevector equals the output wavevector. Its degree is ∑j​(pj​+qj​). Thus an integer vector d=p−q contributes at degree N exactly when the wavevector equation holds, ∥d∥1​≤N, and N−∥d∥1​ is even. The extra even degree is supplied by factors ∣Aj​∣2. This finite integer test distinguishes regular saturation terms from phase-sensitive resonance terms.

Cubic equivariants of the full cube symmetry group (x˙i​=μxi​+axi3​+bxi​∑j=i​xj2​+⋯)

Words: 69
Equivariant dynamical system OurBigBook.com
Independent coordinate reflections require the ith component to be odd in xi​ and even in every other coordinate. Permutations force the same two cubic coefficients in all components. Absolute irreducibility forces a scalar linear coefficient, which can be normalized to the transverse bifurcation parameter. No quadratic terms occur. The axial branches with one, two or three equal nonzero absolute coordinates have leading squared amplitude −μ/[a+(m−1)b], provided that denominator is nonzero.

Equivariant Hopf theorem

Words: 484 Articles: 7
Equivariant dynamical system OurBigBook.com
At a nondegenerate equivariant Hopf bifurcation, each complex axial isotropy subgroup of the spatial group combined with temporal phase gives a branch of periodic solutions with that spatiotemporal symmetry. Assumptions include an isolated semisimple imaginary critical pair of the required representation type, transverse parameter crossing, and a nonzero cubic coefficient on the fixed-point plane. The statement guarantees existence and symmetry type, not stability or which parameter side contains every branch.

Rotating-wave branch of an equivariant Hopf bifurcation

Words: 39
Equivariant Hopf theorem OurBigBook.com
A primary periodic branch whose phase advance is compensated by a spatial rotation. For the natural plane representation, the spatial pattern rotates rather than remaining on a fixed reflection axis. Opposite chiralities are exchanged by reflection.

Adler phase equation OurBigBook.com
A phase that continues winding rather than tending to a locked value. In the noise-free Adler phase equation, ω>ϵ>0 makes the drift positive at every phase, so there are no equilibrium points. The associated tilted washboard potential decreases monotonically; wells vanish at the locking threshold.

Dynamical systems OurBigBook.com
For a weak perturbation of a planar Hamiltonian system, integrate the first-order change of the unperturbed Hamiltonian around each unperturbed periodic orbit. Zeros of this averaged energy drift select candidate perturbed periodic orbits, and a change from positive to negative drift indicates stability.

Area-preserving map (∣detDF∣=1)

Words: 133 Articles: 1
Discrete dynamical system OurBigBook.com
A planar diffeomorphism is area-preserving if the phase-space area of every measurable set is unchanged. The change-of-variables formula proves this property when ∣detDF∣=1 everywhere, and conversely gives that determinant condition for a smooth map preserving all sufficiently small areas. Such a map cannot have an asymptotically attracting fixed point with a positive-area local basin: iterates of a small invariant neighborhood would have to enter arbitrarily small disks while retaining its phase-space area. For a map with constant positive determinant b, invariance of a bounded region of positive phase-space area instead forces b=1.

Their composition preserves area even when the shifts are nonlinear, as in the logarithmic area-preserving seasonal predator-prey map.

Unimodal interval map

Words: 440 Articles: 6
Interval map OurBigBook.com
A unimodal interval map is a interval map that is increasing to one turning point and decreasing afterwards. For a differentiable map with a maximum at zero, a critical point of even order d means f(x)=f(0)+cxd+o(xd) with c<0. The critical order distinguishes universality classes of period-doubling cascades.

Period-doubling renormalization operator OurBigBook.com
Fix R>1 and write h(z)=∑n≥0​hn​((z−1)/R)n with absolutely summable real coefficients. The coefficient space is a Banach space under ∥h∥=∑n​∣hn​∣. The normalized even maps p(x)=1−x2h(x2) form an affine copy of that space and are analytic where ∣x2−1∣<R. On any smaller coefficient disk, the tail beyond degree N is bounded by qN+1∑n>N​∣hn​∣ for a radius ratio q<1. Analytic composition and Cauchy estimates on smaller domains permit certified derivative and truncation bounds. A small ball about an admissible map must additionally preserve the quadratic critical maximum and restrictive-interval conditions; the coefficient norm alone does not impose them.

Itinerary of an interval map

Period three implies all periods
Words: 166 Articles: 1
Interval covering relation OurBigBook.com
For a continuous function from an interval to itself with a three-cycle a<b<c, reflection if needed gives F(a)=b,F(b)=c,F(c)=a. Set I=[a,b],J=[b,c]. The intermediate value theorem gives F(I)⊇J and F(J)⊇I∪J. Successive closed-interval pullbacks realize every cyclic covering word by a point fixed under the corresponding iterate. The word IJn−1 has a unique visit to the interior of I per cycle, forcing least period n; the only boundary ambiguity is the original three-cycle, which realizes n=3 and cannot realize any other such word. A covering of J by itself also gives a fixed point. Thus every positive least period occurs.

Counting cycles in an interval covering graph OurBigBook.com
A five-cycle whose points are in orbit order along the real line gives four interval vertices with arrows 0→1→2→3 and 3→0,1,2,3. A generalized flip is a codimension-two period-doubling point with a simple multiplier −1, a vanishing cubic coefficient in its scalar centre-manifold map, and a nonzero quintic coefficient. Odd symmetry removes even center-manifold jets

Words: 95
Center manifold OurBigBook.com
An odd smooth vector field with a nilpotent center block and an invertible stable block has zero even homogeneous jets in a symmetry-compatible center manifold. At degree two its invariance equation has the form (N−S)h2​=0, where N is the nilpotent differentiation operator generated by the center block and S the invertible stable linear operator. Since their spectra are disjoint, this operator is invertible, so h2​=0. The same argument applies inductively to even orders after lower even jets vanish. This is a statement about local Taylor jets; it does not assert uniqueness of a global center manifold.

Suppose a interval map F:A→A maps every nondegenerate subinterval onto A after finitely many iterates. Three-cycle forces a two-iterate interval horseshoe

Words: 78
Horseshoe for an interval map OurBigBook.com
For a continuous interval map F with a three-cycle a<b<c, after reflecting the coordinate if needed its ordering is F(a)=b, F(b)=c, F(c)=a. Then F2(a)=c, F2(b)=a. Also the intermediate value theorem gives d∈(b,c) with F(d)=b, hence F2(d)=c. Each of [a,b] and [b,d] therefore maps across [a,c] under F2. Choose first-passage subintervals between endpoint levels to avoid overshoots; their interiors are disjoint and both map exactly onto (a,c). This is a horseshoe for an interval map, and establishes Glendinning chaos.

Bifurcation theory studies qualitative changes in equilibria and invariant sets as parameters vary.

Bifurcation parameter

Words: 52
Bifurcation theory OurBigBook.com
A bifurcation parameter labels a family of dynamical systems in which a qualitative change of equilibria or other invariant sets is studied. Near a simple critical eigenvalue crossing, a nonzero derivative with respect to the physical control parameter permits using that eigenvalue itself as a local parameter. At a codimension-two bifurcation, two independent parameters are generally needed.

Global bifurcation

Words: 70
Bifurcation theory OurBigBook.com
A global bifurcation changes an invariant set through a global orbit connection or collision that cannot be identified by a single equilibrium point's linearization alone. For example, a global bifurcation through a saddle homoclinic orbit occurs when an outgoing unstable separatrix returns to the same saddle equilibrium's stable manifold. A smooth global Poincaré return map then combines with a local passage map to determine which side contains a periodic orbit. A heteroclinic orbit instead joins distinct equilibrium points; an energy-balance or Melnikov integral can locate its breaking in a nearly Hamiltonian system.

Words: 211 Articles: 2
Bifurcation theory OurBigBook.com
A Neimark–Sacker bifurcation of a smooth planar map occurs when a simple complex-conjugate pair of fixed-point Floquet multipliers crosses the unit circle away from low-order resonances. If its radial normal form is r′=r(1+η+dr2)+⋯ with d=0, a small invariant closed curve has r2=−η/d+⋯. For d<0 it appears on η>0, where the fixed point has become unstable, and its radial Floquet multiplier is 1−2η+⋯, so the bifurcation is supercritical. For d>0 the curve lies on η<0 and is unstable, giving a subcritical bifurcation. Area-preserving maps have a vanishing cubic radial drift at an elliptic point and do not meet this dissipative nondegeneracy condition.

Bifurcation theory OurBigBook.com
A change in local branches or stability of equilibrium points of a dynamical system as a parameter varies. A zero Jacobian eigenvalue is necessary for the equilibrium-branch bifurcations of a smooth finite-dimensional system: without it, the implicit function theorem gives a unique nearby equilibrium branch. It is not sufficient by itself; nonzero coefficients in the reduced normal form of a dynamical system establish the bifurcation type. A Hopf crossing has nonzero imaginary eigenvalues and is a different local bifurcation.

Bifurcation theory OurBigBook.com
A subcritical branch emerges on the parameter side where the original state remains stable. In the cubic Landau amplitude equation A˙=μA−g∣A∣2A with g<0, the small nonzero branch lies at μ<0 and is unstable to radial amplitude perturbations. Higher-order saturation can generate a finite-amplitude stable branch and hysteresis, but this does not follow from a cubic truncation alone.

Supercritical bifurcation

Bifurcation theory OurBigBook.com

In the cubic Landau amplitude equation A˙=μA−g∣A∣2A with g>0, the nonzero branch ∣A∣2=μ/g lies at μ>0 and is stable to radial amplitude perturbations. Continuous phase symmetry still leaves a neutral phase direction. The direction of a branch and its stability should both be checked in a general problem of bifurcation theory.

A limit cycle is an isolated periodic orbit of a dynamical system. It is attracting if nearby orbits approach it in forward time. A continuous family of closed orbits around a center equilibrium does not consist of limit cycles, because its members are not isolated.

r2(t)=1+(r0−2​−1)e−2(t−t0​)1​.

Saddle fixed point of a map (∣λs​∣<1<∣λu​∣)

Words: 94
Fixed point stability for an iteration OurBigBook.com
A planar map has a hyperbolic saddle fixed point when one Jacobian multiplier has modulus less than one and the other has modulus greater than one. In diagonal coordinates the corresponding linear iterates contract and expand geometrically. For a smooth local diffeomorphism, this splitting continues to local stable and unstable manifolds. It differs from the determinant-negative test for a planar continuous flow: an area-preserving map can have a saddle with positive determinant one, because its multipliers can be real reciprocal numbers. The criterion uses the unit circle, not the sign of the real parts.

Cubic population iteration (un+1​=λun​(1−un2​))

Words: 66
Fixed point stability for an iteration OurBigBook.com
The fixed points of this cubic iteration of a map satisfy u=0 or u2=1−1/λ. The nonzero real pair exists for λ<0 or λ>1. Its derivative multipliers are λ at zero and 3−2λ at either nonzero point. The fixed point stability for an iteration criterion therefore proves local asymptotic stability of zero for −1<λ<1 and of the nonzero pair for 1<λ<2. A multiplier of modulus one requires a nonlinear argument rather than this strict derivative test.

Stability threshold of a discrete exponential predator-prey model (rlogr=r−b)

Words: 72
Linear stability OurBigBook.com
For n′=rne−p and p′=n(1−be−p), with 0<b<1<r, the positive equilibrium is pc​=logr, nc​=rlogr/(r−b). Its Jacobian has trace 1+bnc​/r and determinant nc​. The unit-disc root conditions reduce to nc​<1. At nc​=1 the roots form a nonreal conjugate pair and cross the unit circle; their argument satisfies 2cosθ=1+b/r. The unique threshold lies between one and e because nc​ increases strictly and logr=1−b/r<1 at threshold.

Stability matrix (J=Df(x∗​))

Words: 58
Linear stability OurBigBook.com
For x˙=f(x) near an equilibrium point, the stability matrix is the Jacobian matrix of the vector field evaluated at that point. Perturbations obey η˙​=Jη to first order. Its eigenvalues determine linear growth and decay: strictly negative real parts imply local asymptotic stability, while a positive real part gives instability. Zero real parts require further analysis. The stability matrix of a renormalization-group fixed point applies this construction to beta-function flows.

Saddle-centre equilibrium

Words: 46
Linear stability OurBigBook.com
A conservative equilibrium with one real pair of linear eigenvalues ±λ and one imaginary pair ±iω has saddle and centre directions. Generic perturbations have an exponentially growing component, even though finely chosen initial conditions can remain in the centre-stable subspace. The local L2 Lagrange point dynamics is an example.

Sideband instability

Words: 227 Articles: 3
Linear stability OurBigBook.com
A sideband instability is growth of disturbances with wavenumbers slightly displaced from a carrier pattern's wavenumber. A real physical perturbation uses the displaced mode together with its complex conjugate; a complex amplitude equation can couple those two sidebands through its cubic term. The Eckhaus instability is a longitudinal phase-modulation example.
Bloch stability operator (L(q)=e−iq⋅xLeiq⋅x)
Words: 132 Articles: 1
Sideband instability OurBigBook.com
For a spatially periodic nonlinear pattern, a linear stability disturbance is written eλt+iq⋅xv(x) with v periodic on the pattern cell. The conjugated operator L(q) acts on that fixed cell and determines the sideband eigenvalues. Translation invariance supplies zero eigenfunctions at q=0, namely spatial derivatives of the base pattern. Their small-q eigenvalues determine long-wavelength phase stability; other parts of the spectrum can give independent instabilities.
Phase-diffusion coefficient from a Bloch cell problem (D=⟨w,L2​v0​+L1​v1​⟩)
Words: 69
Bloch stability operator OurBigBook.com
Suppose a Bloch stability operator has expansion L(q)=L0​+iqL1​−q2L2​+⋯, with a simple neutral eigenfunction v0​ and an adjoint neutral function w normalized by ⟨w,v0​⟩=1. Expand v(q)=v0​+iqv1​+⋯ and λ(q)=icq−Dq2+⋯. The Fredholm alternative gives c=⟨w,L1​v0​⟩ and the cell problem L0​v1​=cv0​−L1​v0​, ⟨w,v1​⟩=0. Applying the adjoint solvability condition at second order gives the displayed phase-diffusion coefficient. Multiple translation phases or a conserved mean require a coupled matrix problem rather than this scalar formula.

A spatial sideband is a Fourier perturbation with wavenumber close to a pattern's carrier wavenumber, such as kc​+p or kc​−p. A real physical field also includes the conjugate Fourier component. Linearizing a nonlinear complex amplitude equation can couple the two displaced components, so testing only a single uniform amplitude misses their joint linear stability problem.

Lyapunov functional

Words: 182 Articles: 2
Lyapunov function OurBigBook.com
A Lyapunov functional assigns a scalar to the entire state of an evolution equation and is monotone along its trajectories. For a gradient flow AT​=δV/δA, the identity dV/dT=2∫∣AT​∣2 follows from the variational chain rule, with boundary terms removed by periodicity or decay. A spatial density is not itself a Lyapunov functional unless all remaining coordinates are integrated or averaged.

Words: 123 Articles: 1
Lyapunov functional OurBigBook.com
For the conserved-mean convection amplitude equations before amplitude reduction, the functional V=⟨μ∣∇T∣2/2−(ΔT)2/2−∣∇T∣4/4⟩ generates a gradient flow with increasing V. Periodic integration by parts identifies its variational gradient with the evolution equation. Completing the square gives V=μ2/4−⟨(∣∇T∣2−μ)2/4+(ΔT)2/2⟩≤μ2/4. Hence ∫0∞​⟨Tt2​⟩dt<∞ along a globally smooth solution. Under compactness of the orbit, its limiting states are stationary; a nonstationary periodic orbit is impossible.

Increasing-gradient functional for poorly conducting convection OurBigBook.com
A nonconstant smooth periodic roll obeys μ⟨T0′2​⟩−⟨T0′′2​⟩−⟨T0′4​⟩=0. The orthogonal-roll perturbation raises the increasing-gradient functional for poorly conducting convection by the displayed amount. The variance is strictly positive: a nonconstant periodic function has a derivative that vanishes somewhere and is nonzero somewhere. The Hessian of V therefore has a positive direction. Its self-adjoint linearized evolution operator has a positive Rayleigh quotient and hence a positive eigenvalue, proving transverse linear instability wherever a nonconstant roll exists.

For x˙=x(1−y) and y˙​=x2−y, on either half-plane x=0 the Lyapunov function L is nonnegative, has compact sublevel sets contained in that half-plane, and satisfies L˙=−2(y−1)2. The only invariant points of {y=1} are (1,1) and (−1,1). The invariance argument therefore makes each half-plane converge to its corresponding stable focus. The stable set of the saddle at (0,0) is exactly the line x=0.

An equilibrium is Lyapunov stable if every neighbourhood contains a smaller neighbourhood whose forward trajectories remain in the original neighbourhood for all time.

Orbital stability

Lyapunov stability OurBigBook.com
Orbital stability asks that a disturbance remain close to an invariant orbit or symmetry family, rather than to one fixed representative. In a complex Landau amplitude equation with β=0, μ>0, λ>0, the circle ∣A∣=μ/λ​ attracts radial disturbances while every phase on it remains stationary. The family is attracting as a set, but its individual points do not have individual asymptotic stability because their phase is neutral.

First Lyapunov theorem

Words: 67
Lyapunov function OurBigBook.com
A positive-definite Lyapunov function with nonpositive orbital derivative proves Lyapunov stability of the equilibrium. Indeed, fix a sufficiently small ball Bε​ in the function's domain and put
α=min∥x∥=ε​V(x)>0.
(56)
Continuity and V(0)=0 give a ball Bδ​ on which V<α. Since V cannot increase along a trajectory, one starting in Bδ​ cannot cross the sphere ∥x∥=ε, on which V≥α. It therefore remains in Bε​ for all forward time.

An equilibrium is asymptotically stable when it is Lyapunov stable and every trajectory starting sufficiently nearby converges to it.

Quasi-asymptotic stability

Words: 57
Asymptotic stability OurBigBook.com
An equilibrium point is quasi-asymptotically stable when some neighborhood of initial conditions has forward solutions converging to it. This attraction condition alone does not include Lyapunov stability. Asymptotic stability requires both attraction and Lyapunov stability. A positive Lyapunov function with nonpositive derivative and no nonstationary invariant trajectory in its zero-derivative set proves both when its sufficiently small sublevel sets are compact and forward invariant.

For e˙=Ae, differentiation gives d∥e∥2/dt=eT(A+AT)e. A uniform negative-definiteness bound with κ>0 yields exponential contraction by direct integration of this differential inequality. This is a sufficient criterion for asymptotic stability, stronger than requiring all eigenvalues of A to have negative real parts. A merely semidefinite symmetric part needs additional analysis.

Words: 54
Asymptotic stability OurBigBook.com
A Hurwitz stable matrix has all eigenvalues strictly in the open left half-plane. For x˙=Ax, this is equivalent to eAtx→0 for every initial vector. Jordan blocks contribute polynomial factors times eλt, which decay exactly when their eigenvalues have negative real part. Translating an affine equilibrium reduces its attractivity to this same condition.

Compact gradient-flow trapping criterion (V˙=−∥∇V∥2)

Words: 69
Invariant sublevel set OurBigBook.com
A smooth gradient flow confined to a compact invariant sublevel set has finite total integral of ∥∇V∥2 when V is bounded below. Compactness supplies uniform continuity of that squared norm along the trajectory, so it tends to zero. Every accumulation point is a critical point. If the trapped component contains exactly one critical point, the trajectory converges to it. This supplies a direct convergence proof in place of an inference solely from an energy-contour picture.

The largest such component supplies the strongest basin estimate available from that Lyapunov function alone.

Hartman-Grobman theorem

Words: 81
Hyperbolic equilibrium point OurBigBook.com
For a continuously differentiable dynamical system x˙=f(x), a fixed point is hyperbolic if no eigenvalue of its Jacobian has zero real part. In a neighborhood of a hyperbolic fixed point, the nonlinear flow is locally topologically conjugate to its linearized flow. Thus the saddle, attracting or repelling character persists under the nonlinear terms. The theorem does not decide the nonlinear character of an equilibrium with purely imaginary or zero eigenvalues: a conserved Hamiltonian, Lyapunov function or higher-order analysis may be needed instead.

A trapping region is a compact region across whose boundary the vector field points inward. It is positively invariant and confines every forward trajectory that enters it.
This is a dynamical example of an invariant; forward invariance and strict inward trapping are additional conditions.

A steady state is a state whose observable description is independent of time. In a transport problem it can sustain nonzero fluxes even though local fields remain time independent.
